The malvi\-speaking people of madhya pradesh and rajasthan: a sociolinguistic profile\.
SIL Electronic Survey Report 2009\-011, SIL International, Dallas, Texas, 9 2009\.
The report states that schwa, turned a, turned v and alpha are used interchangeably and assumes no phonemic distinction among them\. Source IPA remains in Original/Phonemic while a dedicated display profile applies Jambu conventions\. Lexical\-similarity category numbers and letters are retained only in Notes and do not assert historical cognacy\. Thirty\-four used legacy CIDs were resolved without OCR: thirty\-one from the report's own IPA chart and three from the official SAG\-IPA conversion table plus rendered\-page checks\. The Thillorkhurd extraction was independently compared to its later Unicode reprint in ESR 2012\-002, with 132 exact response matches across 126 concepts\. The report states that schwa, turned a, turned v and alpha are used interchangeably and assumes no phonemic distinction among them\. Source IPA remains in Original/Phonemic while a dedicated display profile applies Jambu conventions\. Lexical\-similarity category numbers and letters are retained only in Notes and do not assert historical cognacy\. Thirty\-four used legacy CIDs were resolved without OCR: thirty\-one from the report's own IPA chart and three from the official SAG\-IPA conversion table plus rendered\-page checks\. The malvi\-speaking people of madhya pradesh and rajasthan: a sociolinguistic profile\.
SIL Electronic Survey Report 2009\-011, SIL International, Dallas, Texas, 9 2009\.
The report states that schwa, turned a, turned v and alpha are used interchangeably and assumes no phonemic distinction among them\. Source IPA remains in Original/Phonemic while a dedicated display profile applies Jambu conventions\. Lexical\-similarity category numbers and letters are retained only in Notes and do not assert historical cognacy\. Thirty\-four used legacy CIDs were resolved without OCR: thirty\-one from the report's own IPA chart and three from the official SAG\-IPA conversion table plus rendered\-page checks\. The Thillorkhurd extraction was independently compared to its later Unicode reprint in ESR 2012\-002, with 132 exact response matches across 126 concepts\. Printed source metadata provide localities and administrative units but no point coordinates, so the thirty dialect rows intentionally leave coordinates blank\.
URL: [http://www\-01\.sil\.org/silesr/2009/silesr2009\-011\.pdf](http://www-01.sil.org/silesr/2009/silesr2009-011.pdf)\.
references.progress: Appendix B, printed pages 59--177: 6,894 lexical responses from thirty Malvi target lists grouped by the source as Ujjaini, Rajwadi, Umadwadi, Sondhwadi, Gond-Malvi and Bhil-Malvi. Excludes 37 target cells printed as "By Name" rather than a lexical form, two Bhili and two Nimadi comparison lists, the Bhopali comparison list, the Hindi, Gujarati and Marathi standards, ten explicit no-entry control cells, and prompts 11 breast, 23 urine and 24 feces which the report says were disqualified and removed
references.provenance: The exact official publisher PDF was recovered through Internet Archive capture 20150930085157 because the legacy SIL URL no longer serves the file directly; PDF SHA-256 e67e314974ab10eb8244b08dba56d08d1ce8cbf16eaef1be022071d49032a2dd. The PDF is not redistributed.
